candidates.title: A 65.1 TOPS/W Digital CIM Processor for Ultra-Low-Bit Transformers with Multiplexer-based Adder and Scaling Factor-based Reordering
candidates.venue: International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
candidates.abstract: As large-language-model (LLM) continues to expand in parameter size and improve performance, challenges related to latency and energy efficiency become increasingly significant. While low-bit weight quantization was proposed to alleviate the external memory access bottleneck, it remains insufficient to reduce overall energy consumption. In this paper, we use binarized LLM and design a novel Computing-in-Memory (CIM) processor to reduce both computation and memory energy. We propose three key techniques: 1) Multiplexer-based adder is proposed to replace first stage adders of adder tree with the simple multiplexers and inverter, reducing adder tree energy consumption by 58%, 2) Scaling factor-based reordering is proposed to reduce adder tree bit-width, resulting in an additional 28.6% energy reduction, 3) Cluster-level broadcasting and bit-spatial mapping is proposed to reduce internal memory access and increase bit-scalability. As a result, we can reduce the overall energy consumption by 69.7%, offering a more efficient solution for LLM inference tasks.
candidates.reason: 二値化LLM向けにマルチプレクサベース加算器で加算ツリーのエネルギーを58％削減し、スケーリング因子ベースの並べ替えでビット幅を削るデジタルCIMプロセッサを設計し65.1 TOPS/Wを達成しており、超低ビットTransformer推論のハードウェア高速化に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: GM-Skip: Metric-Guided Transformer Block Skipping for Efficient Vision-Language Models
candidates.venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
candidates.abstract: Transformer-based Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable success in image captioning, object recognition, and visual reasoning, but their heavy computational overhead limits deployment in latency-sensitive settings such as autonomous driving. We introduce GM-Skip, a flexible and metric-adaptive framework for Transformer block skipping that accelerates VLM inference while preserving task performance. GM-Skip employs a greedy, metric-guided block selection strategy that leverages feedback from evaluation metrics (e.g., accuracy, CIDEr) to identify redundant layers, combined with a reverse-order deletion mechanism that preserves essential early representations. A score-sparsity balance objective further enables controllable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across tasks. Experiments on COCO, CODA, and realworld driving scenarios show that GM-Skip consistently improves inference speed with minimal performance loss. On COCO, it boosts single-object classification accuracy on the Person category by 19.1%-87.3% while skipping over 40% of Transformer blocks, enhances multi-object detection by 23.4% with 35% sparsity, and doubles the captioning quality (CIDEr) of Qwen-VL under comparable latency. When integrated into an autonomous vehicle running Autoware. Universe, GM-Skip achieves up to 45.4% latency reduction in real-world inference, validating its practical effectiveness for efficient, adaptive VLM deployment.
candidates.reason: GM-Skipは指標フィードバックで冗長なTransformerブロックを貪欲に選び逆順削除で基礎ブロックを保ちながら視覚言語モデルの推論を高速化する、疎性と性能のトレードオフを調整可能なブロック・スキッピング枠組みであり、VLM推論の効率化に直接貢献する。
